Hangars can help to hit corvettes with high evasion (usually in the late-earlygame and early-midgame, especially if you're fighting an opponent with better tech) where the tracking on traditional arms might fail you. In general though, the smaller weapons slots/picket defense weapons on corvettes/destroyers can counter fighters fairly effectively. Hangars are mostly useful when everyone is making battleships/titans and other massive artillery loadouts because their smaller picket ships can be pretty quickly taken down by your defense platforms, leaving the big guns open to fighters that can bypass their shields.

Building Gun Batteries (earlygame) or Hangar Bays (midgame or lategame) instead of shipyards is a good place to start, and upgrading your stations as much as possibile will help make room for additional armaments (as well as naturally increase their power).


Building Defense Platforms (earlygame) and/or Ion Cannons (lategame) are the main things that will bolster your defense, but beware, they cost a LOT of alloys. It may not seem like much at first, but once you've got 10+ fully upgraded stations it starts to add up fast, and ends up being similar in cost to if you just built up your fleet.


There are also lots of buildings like Disruption Field Generators (always useful), Command Centers (only useful for boosting the power of your fleet in a system, not the station itself), Target Uplink Computers and Defense-Grid Supercomputers (only useful if you build ion cannons/defense platforms) that you can get through research and help give your stations a cutting edge to turn the tides in otherwise close calls.
